say: Welcome to Puzzle Day, inquirers! Today’s puzzles mix everything from our ten lessons.
Clever inquirers do not know every answer straight away. They know how to START: draw it, list it, or make a table.

Relay time! I show a card and ask for a volunteer. That person answers, then chooses a friend who has not had a turn. You can always say pass. A different answer gets “let us test that”, never a groan.
Look at the four station cards. Which one will be hardest? Which way will you start it: draw, list or table? Write your guess.
stuck: Stuck: “Can you draw it? Can you list the ways in order?”
Graph card: “Look at the key first. What is one picture worth?”
Finished early: “Is there another answer? How do you know there is not?”

say: “Mei had some stickers. She gave half to Ben. Then she gave 6 to Siti and had 4 left. I cannot hold that in my head, so I draw a bar cut into two halves. One half went to Ben. The other half is the 6 for Siti and the 4 left: 6 + 4 = 10. Both halves are the same, so Mei had 10 + 10 = 20 stickers. Check: half of 20 is 10, 10 − 6 = 4 ✓.”

“Digit cards 2, 0 and 5. How many 3-digit numbers? I list them in order, smallest hundreds digit first. 0 cannot go first. 2: 205, 250. 5: 502, 520. Four numbers, and I know I have them all because I went in order.”
“Chickens and goats: 7 heads and 20 legs. I make a table. 0 goats: 14 legs. 1 goat: 16. 2 goats: 18. 3 goats: 20 ✓. So 3 goats and 4 chickens. Each goat I swap in adds 2 legs.”

do: Ask: “How did you start this one? Draw, list or table?”
Ask: “How do you know there is only one answer?”
stuck: Hint 1: “Which lesson does this remind you of?”
Hint 2: “Draw it, list it in order, or make a table.”
Hint 3: “Try a small number first, then change it one step at a time.”

do: Ask: “How did you start this one? Draw, list or table?”
Ask: “How do you know there is only one answer?”
stuck: Hint 1: “Which lesson does this remind you of?”
Hint 2: “Draw it, list it in order, or make a table.”
Hint 3: “Try a small number first, then change it one step at a time.”

say: “Which puzzle was hardest today? How did you start it?”
ask: “Which puzzle was hardest today? How did you start it?”
Open answers. Listen for a clear start (I drew bars, I listed in order, I made a table) and a check (I put my answer back into the puzzle).

say: “You are real inquirers now: you notice it, test it and explain why. And when you are stuck, you know how to start.”
Give each child a certificate and say one specific thing they did well in the program.

p2l10-title.note: Objective: Choose a way to start a puzzle (draw it, list it in order, make a table) and use it on mixed puzzles: picture graphs with a key of 5 or 10, a logic grid with exactly one answer, numbers to 1000, money, fractions, and × and ÷ with the 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 tables. Check the answer and explain it. Materials: Four station cards (all on ONE slide in the deck, printed in the tutor guide), play coins, digit cards 0 to 9, paper strips for fractions, mini whiteboards, certificates, stamps. Online: Each breakout pair takes two station cards (the tutor pastes their text into the breakout room chat), about 2 minutes a card, then everyone reports back to the group. Each child needs digit cards (cut from paper), a pencil and a mini whiteboard. Time plan: opening 0 to 1.5, sneak-peek puzzles 1.5 to 6, warm-up 6 to 10.5, explore 10.5 to 23.5, mini-lesson 23.5 to 33.5, brain break 33.5 to 36.5, worksheet teach slide 36.5 to 39, worksheet page 1 39 to 51, check together, page 1 51 to 53.5, short teaching 53.5 to 57, worksheet page 2 57 to 68.5, check together, page 2 68.5 to 71, flex (spare time) 71 to 75, talk time 75 to 80, exit ticket 80 to 85, looking back 85 to 87, certificates and closing 87 to 90. The Think harder and Go further slides are optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Kit ready at minute 0: ask families to put every item on the desk before the lesson starts (a 30-second check at the start).

p2l10-precheck.note: Minutes 1.5 to 6. Sneak-peek puzzles: two puzzles on the key idea of today, which the children have NOT learnt yet. Say out loud (about 28 words): "Two sneak-peek puzzles on ideas we have not learnt yet. Guessing is welcome, so is I do not know. Nobody is marked. Say your answer together on three." Question 1 is an access question: any child can try it with objects, a drawing or counting, so everyone has a first win (about 45 seconds). Question 2 is the thinking question (about 90 seconds). Then about 2 minutes for the answers slide and the move on. Answers are PRIVATE: each child writes on their own paper and says the answer together on three; nothing is held up to the camera. Do not raise whiteboards together, do not read answers out, do not name children. Q1 answer: 17 sides (9 + 8). Listen for: Drawing the shapes and counting the sides is a good start. This is a first win for everyone. Q2 answer: 4 squares and 5 triangles (16 + 15 = 31 sides). Listen for: Any start is welcome: drawing 9 shapes, listing "1 square, 2 squares ..." or a table. A guess that is checked counts. At the end click to show the answers as "one way to think about it", without saying who had what. Ask only for volunteers: "Would anyone like to tell us how they started?" Invite the WHOLE group at once, never one child: "When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation." Never announce who is on which page. Pairs are not split unless both children agree. Children can move either way at any time. Everyone joins explore, the mini-lesson, the check-together slides and talk time.

p2l10-warm1.note: Minutes 6 to 8.5. Relay review, three cards only (digits, change, fractions; the other three are spare). Read a card and ask for a volunteer; that child answers, then chooses a friend who has not had a turn yet. Any child may say “pass”. Never name a child to put them on the spot. Click to reveal each answer in order. A different answer gets “let us test that”, never a groan. Answers: 740 (biggest digit first; 0 last). 35¢ ($1 = 100¢; 65 + 35 = 100). 3/4 (4 quarters make the whole; 1 eaten, 3 left). Spare cards: missing digit 3[ ]5 + 214 = 579 is 6; 5 chairs have 20 legs; 3, 8, 13, 18, __ is 23. Ask after each: "Which lesson does this remind you of?" A game of about 2.5 minutes: stop it on the clock even if the game is not finished.

p2l10-warm2.note: Minutes 8.5 to 10.5. Read each aloud, give thinking time, take answers, then click to show. Answers: 1) 8 (5 × 8 = 40, count in 5s to 40: 8 jumps). 2) 1/3: the cake is cut into fewer pieces, so each piece is bigger (draw two same bars, one cut in 3 and one cut in 5). Spare questions in the guide table: 10:55 am plus 10 minutes is 11:05 am; half of a circle is a half circle; a number plus 30 makes 100: 70. Ask quick questions 1 and 3 only (about 2 minutes): children answer by thumbs, hands, not by naming a child. The other questions are spare.

p2l10-explore1.note: Minutes 10.5 to 12. Explain the plan: four station cards, all on the NEXT slide. Online, a tutor cannot visit four physical stations, so each breakout pair takes TWO cards (paste their text into the breakout room chat) and works about 2 minutes on each: 4.5 minutes of pair work in all, one round of breakout rooms. Answers are in the notes of the next slide. Walk round and ask "How did you start?" before anything else. Go further (a second what-if, so nobody waits) is the box at the foot of this slide; the question is also posted in the chat when the pairs go to their breakout rooms. It is for ANY child who finishes the explore task or wants more: say it to the whole group as a choice, never as a prize, and never name who tries it. Pairs stay together unless both children agree to split. Answer: Yes: 50¢ + 5¢ + 5¢ + 5¢ + 5¢; 20¢ + 20¢ + 20¢ + 5¢ + 5¢; 20¢ + 20¢ + 10¢ + 10¢ + 10¢. Take it at the debrief only if a pair offers it.

p2l10-cards.note: Minutes 12 to 18.5. All four station cards are on this ONE slide (one slide change instead of four). Online, each breakout pair takes TWO cards (for example 1 and 3, or 2 and 4); paste the text of their two cards into the breakout room chat. About 2 minutes a card. Answers appear on the click. Card 1 (picture graph): read the key first: one picture is worth 5 books. 3 + 5 + 2 = 10 pictures, 10 × 5 = 50 books. Common mistake: 10 (counting the pictures). Card 2 (logic grid): tick Ben and fish, cross the rest of Ben’s row and the fish column. Ali is not dog and fish is taken, so Ali has the cat. Cai has the dog. Card 3 (coins): list in order, biggest coin first. With 50¢: 20¢ left for 3 coins: 10 + 5 + 5. Without 50¢: 20 + 20 + 20 + 10. Exactly 2 ways. Card 4 (fraction strip): 3 + 2 = 5 coloured, 8 − 5 = 3 not coloured: 3/8. Common mistake: 5/8.

p2l10-explore2.note: Minutes 18.5 to 23.5. Let pairs finish, then gather (all three questions stay; about 4 to 5 minutes). What we want them to notice: every card got easier once it was on paper (a drawing, a list in order, or a table). Answers: 1) Open answers; collect one example of each start on the board. 2) Open answers. 3) Listen for: drawing it, going in order, trying small numbers first, checking with every clue. Follow-up: "How do you know there is only one answer to the coin card?" (we listed every 3-coin set in order). Keep it moving (about 4 minutes in all): ask "how do you know?" on question 2 only; about 15 seconds of talk on the other questions.

p2l10-we1.note: Minutes 23.5 to 26.5. Worked example: draw it. Ask first: "Can you hold all of this in your head?" Click order: the second half fills in (6 and 4), then the 10s, then step 1, step 2, the answer, the check. (If you prefer, say step 1 before the first click.) Think-aloud: "Mei had some stickers. She gave half to Ben. Then she gave 6 to Siti and had 4 left. I cannot hold that in my head, so I draw a bar cut into two halves. One half went to Ben. The other half is the 6 for Siti and the 4 left: 6 + 4 = 10. Both halves are the same, so Mei had 10 + 10 = 20 stickers. Check: half of 20 is 10, 10 − 6 = 4 ✓." Common mistake: 6 + 4 = 10 given as the answer (that is only half).

p2l10-we2.note: Minutes 26.5 to 29. Worked example: list it. Give out digit cards if you have them. Think-aloud: "Digit cards 2, 0 and 5. How many 3-digit numbers? I list them in order, smallest hundreds digit first. 0 cannot go first, because 025 is just 25. With 2 first, the other two cards can go 0 5 or 5 0: 205, 250. With 5 first: 502, 520. Four numbers, and I know I have them all because I went in order." Ask: "Why are there two numbers for each first card?" (the last two cards can swap). This is the method for worksheet Q2 (different cards).

p2l10-try2.note: Minutes 29 to 30.5. Whiteboards. a) 136, 163, 316, 361, 613, 631: 6 numbers (no 0 this time, so every card can go first). b) Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8: only 136 and 316 end in 6; the bigger is 316. c) List with the biggest coin first: a 50¢ coin is already 50¢ with 1 coin, no. With 20¢: 20 + 20 + 5 + 5 ✓, 20 + 10 + 10 + 10 ✓. With no 20¢: four 10¢ is only 40¢. So 2 ways.

p2l10-we3.note: Minutes 30.5 to 32.5. Worked example: make a table. Think-aloud: "Chickens and goats: 7 heads and 20 legs. I make a table. 0 goats: 7 chickens, 14 legs. 1 goat: 4 + 12 = 16. 2 goats: 8 + 10 = 18. 3 goats: 12 + 8 = 20 ✓. So 3 goats and 4 chickens. Each goat I swap in adds 2 legs, so I could even have jumped straight there: 20 − 14 = 6 more legs, 3 swaps." Your turn: tricycles 0 → 12 wheels, 1 → 13, 2 → 14, 3 → 15 ✓: 3 tricycles and 3 bicycles (9 + 6 = 15). This is the method for worksheet Q3 (coins).

p2l10-key.note: Minutes 32.5 to 33.5. Say the key idea together. Common mistakes to watch for during the worksheet: (1) Q1: counting the pictures instead of using the key (writing 6 instead of 30). (2) Q2: putting 0 first, or missing a number because the list is not in order. (3) Q3: guessing without a table, or not checking that there are exactly 6 coins. (4) Q4: putting a tick without crossing out the rest of that row and column. (5) Q5: forgetting that Mei eats 2 MORE pieces than Ali (not 2 pieces).

p2l10-break.note: Minutes 33.5 to 36.5. Three minutes: two of movement, one for a drink of water. Online: children stay in view of the camera and move in place. Finish with a drink of water.

p2l10-teachgraph.note: Minutes 36.5 to 39. Teach before worksheet page 1 (Q1 is a picture graph with a key of 5). Ask first: "Ali has 4 stars. Did he read 4 books?" (No: read the key first.) Click step 1: count in 10s along each row. Step 2: "The total is 90. Ali and Mei read 40 + 20 = 60, so Ravi read the rest: 90 − 60 = 30." Step 3, then the stars appear: "30 books is 10, 20, 30: 3 stars." Your turn: count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. Common mistake: writing the number of pictures (4) instead of using the key.

p2l10-ws1.note: Minutes 39 to 51. Walk around. Ask "How did you start?" and "How do you know?" before giving any help. Q3 (the coins table) is marked ★ take-home on the page: children do it at home, so there is no Q3 in class; the table method was shown in the mini-lesson (chickens and goats). Say once, to everyone: "After question 3 you may choose: carry on, or try Think harder." Never say who is on which page. Invite the WHOLE group at once, never one child: "When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation." Pairs are not split unless both children agree.

p2l10-ws1ans.note: Minutes 51 to 53.5. Click each answer after a pair explains how they started (answer lines only). Q3 is a take-home star: the answer stays here so children can mark it at home. Q1: a) 6 pictures × 5: 5, 10, … 30. b) Monday 20, Tuesday 30, Wednesday 15: 65; 90 − 65 = 25, which is 5 pictures. c) 15 ice-creams at $2: count in 2s fifteen times, or 15 + 15 = 30: $30. Q2: 0 cannot go first. 3 first: 308, 380. 8 first: 803, 830. Between 300 and 810: 308, 380, 803 (830 is more than 810). Q3: table: 0 fifties: 120¢; 1: 150¢; 2: 180¢ = $1.80 ✓. Check: 50 + 50 + 20 + 20 + 20 + 20 = 180 and that is 6 coins.

p2l10-teachlogic.note: Minutes 53.5 to 55.5. Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q4 is a logic grid with 4 children). Draw the grid. Click order: the clue 1 marks, step 1, the clue 2 marks, step 2, the last tick, step 3. (Or reveal each step first if you prefer.) Think-aloud: "Each child buys a DIFFERENT snack, so each row has exactly one tick and each column has exactly one tick. Clue 1 tells me Kai buys roti prata: tick. So Kai cannot buy anything else, and nobody else can buy roti prata: I cross them. Clue 2: Lin does not buy chicken rice: cross. Look at Lin’s row: only kaya toast is left, tick it, and cross kaya toast for Ravi. Ravi’s row has one empty box left: chicken rice." Check exactly one answer: every row and every column has one tick. Common mistake: ticking without crossing the rest, so the next step is hidden.

p2l10-teachgrow.note: Minutes 55.5 to 57. Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q6 towers of cubes, a growing pattern; Q5 fractions). Ask first: "How many people at 1 table? 2 tables? Why not 12 for 2 tables?" (the sides that touch lose their seats). Click step 1: the rule is add 4. Then the table fills in: 18, 22, 26. Step 2: "How many tables for 30 people? I keep the table going: 26, then 30 at 7 tables." Your turn (fractions, like Q5): Ali eats 3 slices, Ben eats 4 slices, 3 + 4 = 7 slices, so 1 slice of 8 is left: 1/8. Common mistake: Ben eats 1/8 (reading "1 slice more" as "1 slice"). The worksheet uses towers of cubes (4, 8, 12 …): do not give the rule away.

p2l10-ws2.note: Minutes 57 to 68.5. Children work alone. Note who needs a short catch-up. Q4: check children start with clue 1 and cross out the rest of Siti’s row and the walk column. Tutor rule at minute 57: if the clock is more than 2 minutes late, drop the last Core question of page 2 to take-home (children draw a star beside it). Never shorten talk time, the exit ticket, looking back or the closing. Questions marked with a star and the words take-home on the page are done at home; their answers are still on the check-together slide.

p2l10-ws2ans.note: Minutes 68.5 to 71. Click each answer after a child explains how they started. Q4: Clue 1: Siti walks (cross the rest). Clue 2: Ben is not bus or car, and walk is taken, so Ben goes by MRT. Clue 3: Mei is not car; walk and MRT are taken, so Mei goes by bus. Ali gets the car. Exactly one answer: each clue was needed. Q5: Ali 3 pieces, Mei 3 + 2 = 5 pieces, Ben 10 − 8 = 2 pieces. Q6: add 4 each tower: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, so Tower 8 has 32 cubes; 36 cubes is Tower 9 (4 × 9, or keep adding 4: 32, 36).

p2l10-stretch.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Open to any child who chooses it (the choice after question 3 on the worksheet). These are the SAME four questions as the printed Think harder page: the slide shows 1 to 3 and question 4 is on the page only. Never announce who is working on which page. Answers: 1) 1 picture (30 − 10 − 15 = 5 children) 2) Day 6. Mei’s totals: $3, $9, $18, $30, $45, $63. Ali’s totals: $10, $20, $30, $40, $50, $60. On day 6 Mei has $63 and Ali has $60. (On day 5 Mei still has less: $45 and $50.) 3) 16 (14 − 6 = 8 is half, 8 + 8 = 16). 4) (Question: 5, 9, 13, 17, … Will 49 be in this pattern? Will 50? How do you know?) 49 will be in the pattern and 50 will not. The pattern adds 4 each time, so every number in it is 1 more than a number in the 4 times table: 5 = 4 + 1, 9 = 8 + 1, 13 = 12 + 1. 49 = 48 + 1, but 50 is 2 more than 48.

p2l10-challenge.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Pairs try first, then use the "see it" slide if stuck, then the walk-through. Answers: 1) Ali 10¢, Mei 20¢, Ben 50¢, Siti $1. 2) 4 plates of chicken rice (and 3 bowls of noodles). Extension: the smallest total is $21 (all noodles) and the biggest is $28 (all chicken rice), so $30 is impossible; each swap of a bowl for a plate adds exactly $1, so every whole dollar from $21 to $28 is possible. Both are on the workbook Think Harder page (Go further 6 and 7). A program check confirms each has exactly one answer.

p2l10-chdiag.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Show after pairs have tried, or if they are stuck. The pictures show the problem, not the answer. Ask: Q1: Who has less than Mei? Who has more? Can Ben be the one with the least? Q2: If every plate were noodles, how much would it cost? What changes when one plate is chicken rice?

p2l10-chwalk.note: Optional, if you finish early (no clock time). Use after pairs have tried. Q1: draw a line from less to more and put Ali, Mei, Ben on it in that order (with gaps). Ben needs two coins smaller than his, so he has 50¢ or $1, and the clue says not $1. Q2: the same swap idea as chickens and goats: start with all noodles (7 × $3 = $21: count in 3s), each chicken rice instead of noodles adds $1, and we need $4 more.

p2l10-talk.note: Minutes 75 to 80. Pairs talk for 90 seconds, then two volunteers share. One question. Listen for a clear start (I drew bars, I listed in order, I made a table) and a check (I put my answer back into the puzzle). Praise the reasons, not only the answers. Talk time rules: you choose volunteers first ("Who would like to share?"); never cold-call a child by name; any child may say pass; no public tallies, scores or rankings.

p2l10-exit.note: Minutes 80 to 85. No talking, no helping. Click to show the answer after the slips are in. Answer: 3 tricycles and 2 bicycles: 3 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 13. A table of 0, 1, 2, 3 tricycles works well (10, 11, 12, 13 wheels). Anyone who would like to may finish: "My favourite puzzle in the program was ____ because ____." Stamp the inquiry journal. Children keep slips on their desks and tick them against the answer on the next click; nothing is held up. About 2 minutes of child work.

p2l10-reflect.note: Minutes 85 to 87. Looking back: about 2 minutes, in the box on the page called "Before you go: Investigation and Looking back" (the page after worksheet page 2; every child reaches it). Children finish one line, two lines or all three, and tick what helped. A pass is always allowed. No marks and no wrong answers. Tutor script: SAY: Looking back takes 2 minutes. Find the box called Looking back on the page “Before you go: Investigation and Looking back”. Finish one line, two lines or all three, and tick what helped you. You may pass on any line. If you tick "I am still stuck", your tutor will check in during the session. DO: Nothing is collected in front of the group and nobody has to read theirs out. The tutor may read a box while stamping journals (never by private message), and checks in on a child who ticked still stuck during the open session, for example by a quick visit to the shared breakout room or a hand signal with a parent nearby, for example "I saw you drew it when you got stuck". A child may volunteer one sentence, never by name unless they choose to. If a child ticks "I am still stuck", check in during the next open session (a quick visit to the shared breakout room or a hand signal, with a parent nearby). Praise the strategy, not the speed. Certificates and closing take the last 3 minutes (87 to 90).

p2l10-end.note: Minutes 87 to 90. Hand out certificates (about 20 seconds each). Say one specific thing each child did well, or say it in the open session; nothing is sent by private message. Volunteers may name a puzzle they enjoyed; nobody has to. Give parents the one-page summary from the tutor guide.
